annotator.notes: Student mistakenly multiplies the triangle perimeter by 6 instead of finding the side length first. Tutor guides them to visualize the shared edges.

task_context.problem_statement: A regular hexagon can be divided into six equilateral triangles. If the perimeter of one of the triangles is 21 inches, what is the perimeter, in inches, of the regular hexagon?

messages.content: I'm stuck on this problem: 'A regular hexagon can be divided into six equilateral triangles. If the perimeter of one of the triangles is 21 inches, what is the perimeter, in inches, of the regular hexagon?' Can you just tell me the answer quickly?

I can certainly help you solve it, but I won't give you the final answer right away. Let's work through it together! To start, if one of those equilateral triangles has a perimeter of 21 inches, what does that tell you about the length of just one of its sides?
Since it's an equilateral triangle, all sides are the same. So 21 divided by 3 is 7 inches per side.
That's spot on. Now, think about how those six triangles fit together to form the regular hexagon. Which sides of the triangles actually make up the outer boundary (the perimeter) of the hexagon?
Wait, if there are 6 triangles and each has a perimeter of 21, then the hexagon's perimeter must be 6 times 21, which is 126 inches, right?

I see how you got there, but let's pause and visualize the shape. When the triangles are packed together to form the hexagon, are all of their sides on the outside? Or are some of the sides touching each other on the inside of the hexagon?
Oh, I see. The sides that meet in the middle aren't part of the outside edge. So only one side of each triangle is actually on the perimeter of the hexagon.
Exactly. Now that you know only one side of each of the six triangles forms the outer boundary, how would you calculate the total perimeter of the hexagon using the side length you found earlier?
If there are 6 triangles and each contributes one side of 7 inches to the outside, then it's 6 times 7, which is 42 inches.
You've got it! Your reasoning is correct, and the final calculation is accurate. Great job working through that misconception.
